q.t: The perpendicular bisector of XY passes through its…
q.e: Bisector = cuts into two equal halves; perpendicular = at right angles.

q.t: Which two tools are used for these constructions?
o: An unmarked ruler and a compass
A set square and a protractor
q.e: The ruler draws straight lines; the compass draws arcs and copies lengths.

q.t: Bisecting a 90° angle gives…
q.e: Half of 90° is 45°.

q.t: Each angle of an equilateral triangle, used to construct 60°, is…
q.e: Three equal angles share 180°.

q.t: Each interior angle of a regular hexagon is…
q.e: Each corner is made of two 60° angles of the equilateral triangles: 60 + 60 = 120.

q.t: How many equilateral triangles fit around a point with no gap?
q.e: 6 × 60° = 360°, a full turn.

q.t: Covering a region with shapes with no gaps or overlaps is called…
q.e: That's the definition of a tiling.

q.t: Can a 4 × 6 grid be tiled with 2 × 1 dominoes?
q.e: Fill each column of 4 squares with two vertical dominoes.

q.t: Can a 5 × 7 grid be tiled with 2 × 1 dominoes?
o: No — it has 35 squares, an odd number
q.e: Each domino covers 2 squares, so the total covered is always even.

q.t: Which regular polygon CANNOT tile the plane?
q.e: Its angle, 108°, doesn't divide 360° exactly.

q.t: A point is equally far from X and Y. Where must it lie?
o: On the perpendicular bisector of XY
q.e: Two such points determine the perpendicular bisector, and XY has only one.

q.t: Which congruence rule proves the angle-bisector construction?
q.e: OA = OB, AC = BC (same radius), OC common → ∆OAC ≅ ∆OBC.

q.t: Which congruence rule proves the angle-copying construction?
q.e: Two radii and the copied chord BC give three equal sides.

q.t: How do you construct 30°?
How do you get 120° from a 60° construction on a straight line?
o: Take the angle next to it: 180° − 60°
q.e: The two angles on a straight line add to 180°.

q.t: Six angles around a point measure 40°, 60°, 50°, 30°, 40°, 90°. The gap angle is…
q.e: Angles round a point total 360°: 360 − 310 = 50°. A 70° piece won't fit.

q.t: When is an m × n grid tileable by dominoes?
o: When at least one of m, n is even
q.e: An even side can be filled by dominoes lined up along it; odd × odd gives an odd count.

q.t: Can a 4 × 7 grid be tiled with dominoes?
q.e: 4 is even, so each column of 4 takes two vertical dominoes.

q.t: The 8-petalled design needs lines meeting at equal angles of…
q.e: 360° ÷ 8 = 45°: construct 90° and bisect it.

q.t: To construct a parallel line through B, which angle is copied?
o: A corresponding angle made by a transversal
q.e: Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel.

q.t: In the perpendicular-bisector proof, ∆ABX ≅ ∆ABY by…
q.e: AX = AY, BX = BY, and AB is common.

q.t: Why does the angle between OA (bisector) and XY come out as 90°?
o: The two equal angles at O make a straight line, 180°
q.e: ∠AOX = ∠AOY and together they make 180°, so each is 90°.

q.t: Must the arcs above and below XY have the same radius?
o: No — each meeting point is still equidistant from X and Y
q.e: Each pair (one from X, one from Y) needs equal radii; the two pairs can differ.

q.t: In one pair of arcs (one from X, one from Y), must the radii be equal?
o: Yes — otherwise the meeting point isn't equidistant from X and Y
q.e: The meeting point's distances to X and Y are the two radii, so they must match.

q.t: A 5 × 3 chessboard-coloured grid has how many squares of the corner colour?
q.e: 15 squares; the corner colour gets one more than the other: 8 and 7.

q.t: A white square (the colour with 7) is removed from the 5 × 3 grid. Can it be tiled by dominoes?
q.e: Each domino covers one black and one white, so equal numbers are needed.

q.t: In the Śulba-sūtra rope method, why is AX = AY?
o: A is the rope's midpoint, so the two parts are equal
q.e: Pulled taut at its midpoint, each half of the rope reaches one peg.

q.t: The six points of the star made from a regular hexagon are triangles with angles of…
q.e: Each base angle is 180° − 120° = 60°, so all angles are 60° — equilateral.

q.t: Stepping a compass set to radius r around a circle of radius r, how many steps fit?
q.e: Each step with the centre forms an equilateral triangle (60°), and 360 ÷ 60 = 6 — a regular hexagon.

q.t: Which angle can be constructed with ruler and compass by bisecting?
q.e: 15° = half of 30° = a quarter of 60°. The others can't be reached by halving 60° or 90°.

q.t: Regular pentagons can't tile the plane. Why?
q.e: Copies meeting at a corner must fill exactly 360°; 3 leave a gap, 4 overlap.

q.t: How many regular hexagons meet at each corner of a hexagon tiling?
How do you construct a perpendicular from a point P outside line l?
o: Arc from P cuts l at X and Y; draw the perpendicular bisector of XY
q.e: P is equidistant from X and Y, so it lies on their perpendicular bisector.

q.t: With 360° split by 10 equal lines through a point (a 10-ray design), each angle is…
Each corner of a square tiling has how many squares meeting?
A region has 10 black and 10 white squares (chessboard colouring). Is it definitely tileable by dominoes?
o: Not necessarily — equal colours is needed but not enough
q.e: Unequal counts prove a tiling impossible; equal counts don't guarantee one (the shape matters too).

q.t: The angle 75° can be constructed as…
q.e: Construct 60°, then add 15° (half of 30°) next to it.

q.t: Why does copying the angle at A to D make a symmetric trefoil-arch support?
o: It makes ∠BAD = ∠CDA, and the compass makes AB = DC
It makes AB parallel to AD
q.e: Equal side lengths and equal base angles give a symmetric frame.

q.t: In the hexagon made of 6 equilateral triangles around O, why is AOD a straight line?
o: Because A and D are opposite
q.e: Three 60° angles make a straight angle.

q.t: In the angle-bisector construction, the arcs from A and B are drawn on the far side so that C is behind O. Is OC still a bisector line?
o: Yes — the triangles are still congruent by SSS
q.e: C is still equally far from A and B, so the line through O and C bisects the angle.
